akdamarchurch.name: Akdamar Church
akdamarchurch.slogan: A pink-stone church afloat in a turquoise lake.
akdamarchurch.line: Built 915-921 for King Gagik Artsruni, its walls carry biblical reliefs, David and Goliath among them.

vankalesi.name: Van Fortress
vankalesi.slogan: Urartian rock above Lake Van, best at sunset.
vankalesi.line: A cliff-face inscription of Xerxes the Great, in three languages, still reads almost perfectly 2,500 years on.

ishakpasa.name: Ishak Pasha Palace
ishakpasa.slogan: A hilltop palace with Mount Ararat for a backdrop.
ishakpasa.line: Begun in 1685 and finished in 1784, it blends Ottoman, Persian, Kurdish and Armenian styles.

nemrutcrater.name: Nemrut Crater Lake
nemrutcrater.slogan: Two lakes, one caldera, and hot springs that never freeze.
nemrutcrater.line: Nemrut's caldera is the largest in Turkey; its lake is fed by hot springs, so it does not freeze in winter.

sutcukenan.name: Van Breakfast Street
sutcukenan.slogan: Fifty small plates before ten in the morning.
sutcukenan.line: While other Turkish cities are known for kebab, Van is known for its breakfast; the BBC called it the city that lives for breakfast.
